site.name: aeroiq
site.summary: AeroIQ Fictional API monitoring and observability SaaS (Datadog / Vercel Observability-style). Pages - `index.html` — Overview dashboard. Left rail nav; top bar with org switcher, environment tabs (Production / Staging / Dev), time range (5m / 1h / 24h / 7d), search (⌘K), theme toggle, alert bell; four top KPIs (total requests / error rate / p95 / availability) with sparklines and period-over-period deltas; 24-card endpoint health grid (red cards first), each card with HTTP method + path + health dot + RPS / p95 / error rate; right alerts side panel with 8 active alerts and per-row assign / silence actions; bottom global p50 / p95 / p99 trend line chart. - `endpoint-detail.html` — Endpoint detail. Top: method + path + health badge + linked services + owner avatars; 6 KPIs (RPS / error rate / p50 / p95 / p99 / SLO status); three large trend charts (request volume, latency p50/p95/p99 three lines, error rate); error-grouping panel with status-code / client-version / region tabs; recent error sample table (5 rows including 502 Bad Gateway, 500, 429, 503); related traces list. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPIs (active / new today / mean response / MTTR); filter bar; 12-row alert

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full AeroIQ system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will start by validating the primary dashboard and its global controls, then drill down into the critical endpoint detail page for an unhealthy endpoint. Next, it will assess the alert management and triage flow, followed by evaluating the endpoints list and service map views. Finally, it will verify responsive behavior and accessibility across the identified risk hotspots.
assumptions: Global controls like environment tabs, time range selectors, and org switcher persist and affect data across multiple pages.
Clicking an unhealthy endpoint card on the dashboard navigates to its specific endpoint-detail.html view.
Alert actions like 'Assign' and 'Silence' trigger local UI state changes (e.g., dialog, status update) without a backend.
Navigation links pointing to '#' (Logs, Integrations, Settings) are placeholder dead-ends and will not render new content.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on environment tabs (Production/Staging/Dev) and time range buttons (5m/1h/24h/7d) causing mobile usability issues.
Missing label on the 'Acme Cloud Org' select dropdown, impacting screen reader accessibility.
Alert action buttons ('Assign', 'Silence') in the dashboard side panel may lack sufficient spacing or clear feedback on interaction.
Service map visualization (services.html) may have poor responsiveness or inaccessible interactive nodes on mobile viewports.

phases.title: Dashboard Overview & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate the primary landing experience, data density, and functionality of global controls.
key_checks: Verify KPI sparklines and period-over-period deltas render correctly.
Interact with environment tabs (Production, Staging, Dev) and time range selectors (5m, 1h, 24h, 7d) to check for UI updates.
Test the ⌘K search input for focus, typing, and clearing behavior.
Click the theme toggle (🌓) to ensure light/dark mode switches smoothly.
Click the alert bell (🔔 8) to see if it opens a dropdown or navigates.
Interact with 'Assign' and 'Silence' buttons on the Active Alerts panel.
exit_criteria: Global controls (env, time, theme, search) exercised.
Alert side panel actions interacted with.

phases.title: Endpoint Drill-down & Triage
phases.objective: Validate the critical flow from the dashboard to a failing endpoint's detailed view and error analysis.
key_checks: Click the worst-performing endpoint card (POST /v1/payments) from the dashboard grid to navigate to endpoint-detail.html.
Verify endpoint health badge, SLO status, and owner avatars render correctly.
Check the three trend charts (Request volume, Latency, Error rate) for visibility and legend clarity.
Interact with the Error breakdown tabs (By status code, By client version, By region).
Validate the Recent error samples table for readability and horizontal scrolling behavior.
Ensure global controls (env, time) on the detail page function consistently.
exit_criteria: Navigated successfully from dashboard to endpoint detail.
Charts and error breakdown tabs interacted with.
Data hierarchy and triage information validated.

phases.title: Alert Center & Filtering
phases.objective: Assess the alert management experience, focusing on filtering capabilities and alert status transitions.
key_checks: Navigate to Alerts via the left rail nav and verify the 4 KPIs (Active, New today, Avg response, MTTR).
Test the filter bar: interact with severity, rules, assignees, and status dropdowns.
Use the search input to filter alerts by keyword.
Attempt to change an alert's status or interact with row-level actions if available.
Verify navigation back to dashboard or endpoint detail from an alert row if linked.

phases.title: Endpoints List & Service Map
phases.objective: Evaluate the secondary navigation pages for inventory management and architectural visualization.
key_checks: Navigate to Endpoints page and test service/health/tag filter dropdowns.
Use the 'Search method or path...' input to filter the endpoint table.
Navigate to Service Map and verify the dependency graph renders.
Click on a service node in the Service Map to check for detail popups or navigation.
Switch between Production and Staging environments on the Service Map.
exit_criteria: Service map rendered and nodes clicked.
Environment switching validated on service map.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility Audit
phases.objective: Identify layout breakage, touch target issues, and accessibility barriers on smaller viewports.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check the left rail navigation (hamburger menu behavior).
Validate tap target sizes for environment tabs, time ranges, and alert actions per layout warnings.
Check if the endpoint detail charts and tables are horizontally scrollable or responsively resized.
Verify the alert filter bar stacks correctly or remains usable on mobile.
Assess color contrast and missing label for the org switcher dropdown.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout tested on dashboard, detail, and alerts pages.
Tap target and accessibility warnings from prescan visually confirmed.
Navigation and core flows remain functional on mobile.

coverage_targets.pages: visit all 5 known HTML pages, attempt placeholder pages (#) to confirm dead-ends
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible filters, tabs, search inputs, theme toggle, and environment/time switches
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (dashboard, endpoint detail, alert filters) on mobile viewport

notes: Pay special attention to the small tap targets flagged in the prescan; verify if they cause overlapping or mis-clicks on mobile.
The org switcher lacks a label; check if context is obvious enough visually or if it hampers screen reader usage.
Since this is a static demo, expect that 'Assign' or 'Silence' actions might only trigger visual state changes or modals rather than full data persistence.

ux_notes: Theme toggle button (🌓) has a small tap target of 34x34px, which is below the recommended 44x44px mobile guidance, posing a usability concern for touch devices.

Clicking the theme toggle produced no visible text or URL change in the automated feedback, suggesting either a lack of visual feedback in the test environment or a missing interaction state indicator.
Other top bar buttons (🔔 8, 👤) share the same small 34x34px dimensions, indicating a systemic small tap target issue in the header controls.

ux_notes: Clicking the 'AeroIQ' logo navigated from services.html to index.html, confirming it acts as a global home link rather than a service node detail trigger.
Navigation via the logo is immediate and functional, but the objective to test service node interaction in the dependency graph was missed because the wrong element (logo) was clicked.
Layout warnings persist on the dashboard: left-rail nav links (195x41px) and environment tabs (e.g., Staging 71x28px) are below the 44px mobile tap target guidance.
Org switcher select element (ux-9) lacks an accessible label, posing a medium-severity accessibility issue.

step.objective: Test the 'Assign' button on the Active Alerts panel to verify interaction feedback and assess its small tap target usability
step.success_criteria: Clicking 'Assign' should trigger some visual feedback (status change, dialog, or toast) confirming the action is interactive

result.feedback: No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

The 'Assign' button has a small tap target (57x24px), which is well below the 44px mobile guidance, confirming the objective's concern about small tap target usability.
The org switcher (ux-9) is flagged with a 'missing_input_label' warning of medium severity, indicating an accessibility gap.

ux_notes: Clicking 'Cancel' on the Silence alert dialog successfully closed the modal and restored the dashboard to its normal state, as evidenced by the visible text returning to standard dashboard KPIs and endpoint health data.
The DOM summary still lists 'Silence alert' as a heading, but the dialog is no longer visually blocking the interface, indicating a minor DOM cleanup delay rather than a functional issue.

Layout warnings persist for small tap targets on left rail navigation items (e.g., 195x41px for 📊 Dashboard) and environment tabs (e.g., 91x28px for Production), which will require attention for mobile viewports.
The org switcher (select element) lacks an accessible label (aria-label), posing a medium-severity accessibility issue.
